// 01

QUICK START

Welcome to the Loose Arrows Divisions Engine. Here's how to go from zero to operational in four steps:

01

Get Your Key

Contact your system administrator to receive an API key. They'll assign you the right access tier for your role.

02

Test Your Key

Make a GET request to /division/10/system/health first (no key needed), then to /division/7/vendors with your key header to confirm access.

03

Set Up Data

Create your first contract (Division 2), register your vendors (Division 7), then build your bid pipeline (Division 3).

04

Run the Pipeline

Create a bid → add line items → generate a quote → submit. Your submission document is ready to print.

TIP: The public demo at /demo shows a live view of the system — no key needed. Great for showing stakeholders what the platform does.

// 02

ACCESS TIERS EXPLAINED

Every API key has a tier. Your tier determines what you can see and do. The system enforces this automatically — no trust model required.

OBSERVER
Read-only access
  • View all contracts
  • View all vendors
  • View bids & pipeline
  • View catalog & pricing
  • Cannot create anything
  • Cannot modify anything
  • No bot access
OPERATOR
Full pipeline access
  • Everything Observer can do
  • Create & edit contracts
  • Register & manage vendors
  • Create bids, quotes, submit
  • Manage inventory & orders
  • Division 1–9 full access
  • No bot commands (Div 10)
ARCHITECT
Full system access
  • Everything Operator can do
  • Division 10 bot commands
  • Autonomous intelligence
  • Contract discovery & analysis
  • System-level commands
  • Architect Command Layer
  • Admin key management

NOTE: Tier upgrades must be requested through your administrator. The system cannot self-upgrade tiers.

// 03

USING YOUR API KEY

The Rule: One Header, Every Request

Add your key as X-API-Key in every request to a /division/* endpoint. That's it. No sessions, no cookies, no login flow.

# cURL example GET https://your-app.replit.app/division/7/vendors X-API-Key: la-opr-your-key-here
# POST example — create a vendor POST https://your-app.replit.app/division/7/vendors X-API-Key: la-opr-your-key-here Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme Medical Supply", "categories": ["wound-care", "surgical"], "contactEmail": "orders@acme.com", "status": "active" }

Using Postman

  1. Open Postman → select your request → go to the Headers tab
  2. Add key: X-API-Key / Value: your key string
  3. For POST/PATCH requests, set Content-Type: application/json in Headers and put your JSON in the Body tab → raw → JSON

Using a Browser (Observer only)

Browsers can't easily send custom headers for regular page loads. For read-only browsing, use the dashboard pages at /vendor/dashboard or /operator/dashboard. For API calls from the browser, use the browser console with fetch():

// Browser console fetch('/division/3/bids', { headers: { 'X-API-Key': 'la-obs-your-key' } }).then(r => r.json()).then(console.log)

Key Format Reference

  • Observer keys start with: la-obs-
  • Operator keys start with: la-opr-
  • Architect keys start with: la-arc-

NO KEY NEEDED for: /demo, /guide, /legal, /api, /division/10/system/health, and all dashboard HTML pages.

// 04

BID PIPELINE — FULL WALKTHROUGH

The core workflow of the Divisions Engine. Here's the complete path from a government solicitation to a submitted bid with a generated capability statement.

Step 1 — Register the Contract Opportunity

Every bid needs a contract record (Division 2). This represents the government solicitation you're responding to.

POST /division/2/contracts X-API-Key: la-opr-... { "contractName": "Gallup IHS Medical BPA", "agency": "HHS/IHS — Navajo Area", "naics": "339113", "contractRef": "NOIFCGIMCBPA26003", "periodOfPerformance": "Base + 4 Options", "status": "active" } → Returns: { contractId: "cmXXX...", ... }

Step 2 — Add CLINs to the Contract

Add each Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) with its pricing. These auto-populate into bids.

POST /division/2/contracts/{contractId}/products { "sku": "ETH2960G", "clin": "CLIN-001", "contractPrice": 85.00, "notes": "Sutures — per box" } → Repeat for each CLIN

Step 3 — Register Your Vendor

The vendor represents your company or a supplier submitting the bid (Division 7).

POST /division/7/vendors { "name": "Loose Arrows Supply & Logistics", "categories": ["medical", "surgical"], "contactEmail": "bids@loosearrows.com", "status": "active" } → Returns: { id: "cmXXX...", ... }

Step 4 — Create the Bid

Link the contract and vendor. Line items auto-populate from the contract CLINs, or you can provide them manually.

POST /division/3/bids { "contractId": "cmXXX...", "vendorId": "cmXXX...", "vendorName": "Loose Arrows Supply & Logistics", "notes": "IHS Gallup BPA — Base Year Pricing" } → Returns: { bidId: "cmXXX...", bidRef: "BID-001", status: "DRAFT", ... }

Step 5 — Adjust Pricing (Optional)

If you need to change unit prices before submission:

PATCH /division/3/bids/{bidId}/pricing { "prices": [ { "sku": "ETH2960G", "unitPrice": 82.50, "quantity": 15 } ] }

Step 6 — Submit the Bid

This changes status from DRAFT → SUBMITTED and generates a quote reference automatically.

POST /division/3/bids/{bidId}/submit → Returns: { status: "SUBMITTED", quoteRef: "QUOTE-001", submittedAt: "...", ... }

Step 7 — Get Your Submission Document

This returns a print-ready HTML capability statement and price list for the solicitation.

GET /division/3/bids/{bidId}/submission → Returns: Full HTML document (Ctrl+P to print or save as PDF)

TIP: The submission document automatically includes your vendor info, all CLINs, pricing table, terms & conditions, and a signature block — ready to send to the contracting officer.

// 05

VENDOR MANAGEMENT (DIVISION 7)

List All Vendors

GET /division/7/vendors → Returns array of all vendor records

Create a Vendor

POST /division/7/vendors { "name": "Vendor Name", "categories": ["medical", "surgical"], "capabilities": ["drop-ship", "bulk-order"], "contactEmail": "contact@vendor.com", "performanceNotes": "SDVOSB certified, FSS approved", "status": "active" }

Update a Vendor

PUT /division/7/vendors/{id} { "status": "inactive", "performanceNotes": "Contract ended FY25" }

Link a Vendor to a Contract

POST /division/7/vendors/{id}/attach { "type": "contract", "referenceId": "{contractId}" }

Vendor categories can be anything relevant: medical, surgical, wound-care, office-supplies, it-equipment, etc.

// 06

CONTRACT REGISTRY (DIVISION 2)

Contract Statuses

  • draft — Being set up, not yet open for bids
  • active — Open for bidding, shows in the bid pipeline
  • expired — Period of performance ended
  • cancelled — Solicitation withdrawn

Key Endpoints

GET /division/2/contracts # list all GET /division/2/contracts/{id} # single contract + CLINs POST /division/2/contracts # create new POST /division/2/contracts/{id}/products # add CLIN PATCH /division/2/contracts/{id} # update status/details GET /division/2/contracts/{id}/catalog # view CLIN catalog

TIP: You can look up a contract by its contractRef (e.g. "NOIFCGIMCBPA26003") instead of the internal ID in most endpoints. Both work.

// 07

BIDS & QUOTES (DIVISION 3)

Bid Statuses & What They Mean

  • DRAFT — Being built. Line items and pricing can still be edited.
  • SUBMITTED — Finalized and submitted. No more edits.
  • UNDER_REVIEW — Government is evaluating the bid.
  • AWARDED — You won. Contract awarded.
  • LOST — Another vendor was selected.
  • WITHDRAWN — You pulled the bid before award.

Key Endpoints

GET /division/3/bid-pipeline # active contracts open for bidding GET /division/3/bids # all bids GET /division/3/bids?status=DRAFT # filter by status POST /division/3/bids # create bid POST /division/3/bids/{id}/line-items # replace line items (DRAFT only) PATCH /division/3/bids/{id}/pricing # update prices (pre-award) POST /division/3/bids/{id}/quote # generate quote reference POST /division/3/bids/{id}/submit # DRAFT → SUBMITTED PATCH /division/3/bids/{id}/status # update outcome status GET /division/3/bids/{id}/submission # printable capability statement

Manual Line Items

If you want to set line items manually instead of auto-populating from the contract catalog:

POST /division/3/bids/{id}/line-items { "lineItems": [ { "sku": "ETH2960G", "clin": "CLIN-001", "description": "Sutures", "quantity": 15, "unitPrice": 85.00 }, { "sku": "KCI-T-VAC", "clin": "CLIN-004", "description": "VAC Therapy Kit", "quantity": 3, "unitPrice": 619.50 } ] }
// 08 — ARCHITECT TIER ONLY

DIVISION 10 — AUTONOMOUS BOT

ARCHITECT TIER REQUIRED. All Division 10 bot commands require an Architect-level API key. Observer and Operator keys will be rejected.

What the Bot Does

DIV10-BOT-001 is the autonomous contract intelligence system. It can scan SAM.gov-style feeds for matching solicitations, analyze contract opportunities, and feed intelligence into your bid pipeline — all on command or on a schedule.

Key Bot Endpoints

GET /division/10/bot/status # current bot state (IDLE/RUNNING) POST /division/10/bot/run # trigger a full intelligence cycle GET /division/10/bot/intel # view all discovered intelligence GET /division/10/system/health # system health (public, no key needed)

Architect Command Layer

The Architect Command Layer allows you to issue high-level directives to the bot:

POST /division/10/bot/command { "command": "SCAN_OPPORTUNITIES", "naics": "339113", "agency": "IHS" }

TIP: Check /division/10/system/health first — it shows all division record counts and confirms the system is operational. No key needed for this one.

// 09

DASHBOARDS

Three browser-accessible dashboards give you visual command interfaces. All dashboard HTML pages are public — they load without a key. Live data inside them uses your API key.

  • /demo — Platform overview & pitch page. Share this URL with anyone.
  • /vendor/dashboard — Vendor-facing cockpit. Shows opportunities, workflow status, and compliance.
  • /operator/dashboard — Operator control room. Full system view with tasks, vendors, and performance data.

Division 10 Cockpit

The Division 10 intelligence cockpit is accessible at /division/10/dashboard. It provides a real-time view of the bot's intelligence feed, contract discovery, and system status. Architect access recommended for full functionality.

// 10

ERROR REFERENCE

StatusMeaningFix
401 API key missing or invalid Add X-API-Key: your-key header. Check key is active and correctly typed.
403 Access denied for your tier Observer trying to write? Operator trying to use bot? Request a tier upgrade from your admin.
400 Bad request — missing or invalid data Check the error message. Usually a required field is missing from your JSON body (e.g. contractName, vendorId).
404 Resource not found The ID you used doesn't exist. Use the list endpoint to find valid IDs.
200 Success (GET/PATCH) All good. Data returned in response body.
201 Created (POST) Record created. Response contains the new record including its ID.

Common Error Messages

  • "contractId and vendorId are required" — You're missing one or both when creating a bid.
  • "Cannot edit line items on a SUBMITTED bid" — Bid is locked. Only DRAFT bids can be edited.
  • "Contract not found" — The contractId or contractRef you passed doesn't match any record.
  • "Observer tier is read-only" — You need an Operator key to write data.
  • "Architect tier required for this endpoint" — You need an Architect key for bot/system commands.
// 11

SECURITY BEST PRACTICES

Protect Your Key Like a Password

  • Never paste your API key into a public chat, email, or GitHub repository
  • Don't share your key with teammates — request individual keys from the admin
  • Store your key in a password manager or secure vault, not in a text file
  • If you suspect your key was exposed, contact your admin immediately to revoke it

Using Your Key in Code

Never hardcode your key directly in source code. Use environment variables:

# In your .env file (never commit this file) LA_API_KEY=la-opr-your-key-here # In your code const key = process.env.LA_API_KEY;

What Happens If Your Key Is Compromised

  1. Contact your admin immediately
  2. Admin deactivates your key in seconds via PATCH /admin/keys/{id}/toggle
  3. Admin issues you a new key
  4. You update your environment variables with the new key

Deactivation is instant — the old key stops working the moment it's toggled off.

HTTPS Only in Production

Always use https:// URLs in production to ensure your API key is encrypted in transit. Never make API calls over HTTP in a production environment.

// 12

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q: How do I get an API key?
Contact the system administrator (Loose Arrows Supply & Logistics). They will ask for your name, email, and intended use, then issue you a key at the appropriate access tier.
Q: My key stopped working — what happened?
Your key may have been deactivated by the admin (due to inactivity, security concern, or account change). Contact your admin to check the status or get a new key issued.
Q: Can I use this from Postman / Insomnia / curl?
Yes. Add X-API-Key: your-key as a header in any HTTP client. There's no special SDK required.
Q: Does my data disappear when the server restarts?
No. As of April 2026, all contracts, vendors, bids, and work requests are stored in PostgreSQL and fully persist across restarts and redeployments.
Q: Can I submit a bid to the government directly from this system?
The system generates a print-ready capability statement and price list (GET /division/3/bids/{id}/submission). You then submit that document to the contracting officer via email or the relevant submission portal (e.g. SAM.gov). The system does not submit directly to government agencies.
Q: Is this platform FAR/DFARS compliant?
The platform helps you manage procurement workflows. Compliance with FAR, DFARS, and applicable regulations is your responsibility. See the Government Procurement Notice in our legal documentation.
Q: I need access to the bot / Division 10. How?
Division 10 bot commands require an Architect-level key. Contact your admin and explain your use case. Architect keys are reserved for authorized personnel only.
Q: Can multiple people use the same API key?
Technically yes, but strongly discouraged. If one person's environment is compromised, the key must be revoked for everyone. Request individual keys for each person — the system has no limit on how many keys can be issued.
Q: What does the Vendor Cockpit show?
The Vendor Cockpit (/vendor/dashboard) is a vendor-facing interface showing available contract opportunities, workflow status, documentation requirements, and compliance status.
Q: How do I report a bug or problem?
Contact the system administrator directly. Include the endpoint you were calling, the request body you sent, and the error response you received. Screenshots are helpful.
